title: Mean pollution-score change was near its spatial prediction despite a weak local BOD slope at 178 English river sites
abstract: We tested whether a weak local pollution slope also means a small overall community shift. We used early-trained, held-out composition scores and the same endpoint records at 178 English river sites. From 1991-2000 to 2008-2017, the mean BOD-score shift was 1.16 times its joint spatial prediction. After spatial adjustment for temperature and ammonia, the mean BOD ratio was 1.17, but the local BOD slope ratio was 0.019. In 499 site and three-year-block resamples, central 95% ranges were 0.63-2.96 and -0.36 to 0.33. Their paired difference was 0.59-2.85. Endpoint coverage and region checks retained this contrast. The mean shift was compatible with full spatial transfer. This does not identify pollution control as its cause: common environmental and observation changes can be confounded with time. It shows that weak local transfer alone cannot establish slow overall recovery. These selected family-level records have little endpoint warming and do not establish full thermal tracking. This is a new analysis of an existing river source, not an independent network.

display.caption: The mean pollution-score shift and the local BOD slope gave different transfer ratios in the same endpoint records. Lines show site and three-year-block resampling ranges.
